Both support P053-induced muscle pathology in aged mice (C4-C6, C28-C39). OpenEval notes potential confounding from systemic effects, while peer reviewers describe findings as 'solid' and 'valuable insights' without methodological concerns.

Both support P053 specificity for CERS1 via lipidomics (C23-C25). OpenEval confirms target engagement and compensatory mechanisms, while peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the pharmacological validation.

Perfect agreement on AAV9-mediated CERS1 knockdown effects (C7-C8, C41-C52). Both recognize consistency between genetic and pharmacological approaches. OpenEval notes muscle-specific approach addresses systemic confounding, peer reviewers explicitly endorse the dual approach.

Both support C2C12 cell-autonomous effects (C54-C59). OpenEval emphasizes independence from systemic factors, while peer reviewers accept these as part of 'highly informative and novel findings' without concerns.

Both support C. elegans conservation of CERS1 function (C66-C71). OpenEval emphasizes evolutionary significance, peer reviewers explicitly note the worm data as supporting evidence for conservation.

Both support eQTL identification for Mendelian randomization (C10, C72-C75). OpenEval details genetic instrument quality, while peer reviewers accept the genetic approach as strengthening causal inference.

Both support Mendelian randomization findings (C11-C12, C76-C78). OpenEval notes reliance on self-reported health as limitation, while peer reviewers describe genetic data as providing 'valuable insights' without concerns.
